Pa. House passes bipartisan legislation to regulate artificial intelligence usage in healthcare
Rep. Arvind Venkat
September 30, 2026 | 3:49 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 30 –
The Pennsylvania House today passed bipartisan legislation that would regulate the application of artificial intelligence in healthcare, ensuring that all Pennsylvanians can have confidence that AI is being utilized in a beneficial manner when receiving clinical care or when insurers are reviewing coverage of specific healthcare recommendations, announced the legislation's co-prime sponsors, state Reps. Arvind Venkat, Joe Hogan, Tarik Khan, Bridget Kosierowski and Greg Scott.
House Bill 1925
would provide new regulations for how AI is utilized and reported by insurers, hospitals and clinicians. These groups would need to provide transparency to patients and the public as to how AI is being used in their companies or practice settings.
"The usage of AI is expanding rapidly into nearly every field, and healthcare is no exception," said
Venkat, D-Allegheny
. "As the General Assembly's only physician, I have seen this development take place in real time. It is vital that patients are confident that AI is being used responsibly and effectively in their care. I thank my House colleagues who partnered on this legislation and helped it to pass in a bipartisan manner. Protecting trust in our healthcare system is vital to the safety and future of all Pennsylvanians."
"Patients deserve to know when artificial intelligence is involved in their healthcare, and they should have full confidence that a qualified healthcare professional, not AI or an algorithm, remains responsible and accountable for their care," said
Khan, D-Phila
. "Our bill protects patients by establishing commonsense safeguards and increasing transparency and accountability as AI becomes a bigger part of healthcare."
"AI technology has the potential to make some healthcare processes more streamlined and efficient, but it's important that we stay ahead of its use as it adapts and changes," said
Scott, D-Montgomery
. "Patients deserve full transparency and confidence in their care. These guardrails ensure that when AI is used in the healthcare setting, it's being used responsibly and alongside expert, human care, too."
The legislation would also prevent clinicians from being superseded in their judgment by AI recommendations by requiring human decision-makers to make final decisions for a patient's care based on an individualized assessment if AI is used by insurers, hospitals or clinicians.
"As AI continues to grow as a tool in our lives, steps must be taken to ensure it does not become over-relied on," said
Hogan, R-Bucks
. "I recognize that it can be a valuable tool in medicine, but we must ensure that all final decisions are made by a human doctor. House Bill 1925 puts that regulation in place, ensuring the best care for patients across the Commonwealth."
"As a nurse for 30 years, I believe we need to install guardrails to ensure AI is being used in the most effective way when it comes to making decisions about patients' healthcare," said
Kosierowski, D-Lackawanna
. "This necessary legislation will ensure that experienced healthcare providers oversee AI assessments and make the final decisions concerning a patient's health or healthcare coverage."
To ensure that current laws related to privacy, safety, and anti-discrimination are upheld, H.B. 1925 would also require attestation from insurers to the PA Department of Insurance or PA Department of Human Services and from hospitals and other healthcare facilities to the PA Department of Health on how their required internal governance and use of AI is in compliance with these laws.
House Bill 1925 passed the House by a vote of 144-59. The bill will now move to the state Senate for consideration.

Venkat welcomes over $1.6 million in new local grants
Rep. Arvind Venkat
September 15, 2026 | 10:49 AM
McCANDLESS, Sept. 15 –
State Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, has announced over $1.6 million in grant funding through the Local Share Account program that will benefit seven projects in McCandless, Franklin Park, Hampton Township and Ohio Township.
“This funding will support a wide range of long-needed projects in our community, from infrastructure repairs to investments in our community safety,” Venkat said. “I look forward to seeing these projects come to fruition, and I am proud to work with my legislative colleagues from across our region to get the funding we need back to our local communities.”
The projects supported with this funding include:
$600,000
for water line replacement on Thompson Run Road in McCandless to address a history of frequent breaks and degraded infrastructure.
$300,000
for lighting and security upgrades at Wall Park and Vestal Park in McCandless.
$200,000
for renovations at the Ingomar North Recreation and Swimming Club facility in McCandless, including replacing the pool liner to reduce water loss, installing a new pool vacuum to ensure the longevity of the pool liner and to purchase a new pool cover for winter protection.
$200,000
to replace the roofs of the municipal and FITES building in Hampton Township.
$179,457
to repair aging components of the LaRoche East Dam in McCandless.
$102,698
to Franklin Park Borough for the purchase of a new multipurpose patrol vehicle.
$100,000
to Ross West View EMS Authority, which serves Ohio Township, for the purchase of a new emergency ambulance.
The Franklin Park project was backed by Venkat and state Sen. Devlin Robinson, and all McCandless projects were backed by Venkat and state Sen. Lindsey Williams. Venkat supported the Hampton project alongside Williams and Rep. Jeremy Shaffer, and the Ross West View EMS project alongside Williams, Robinson, and Reps. Lindsay Powell and Emily Kinkead.
The
Local Share Account program
is funded through revenue generated by gaming and are administered by the Commonwealth Financing Authority to support projects that enhance economic development, public infrastructure and community vitality.

Dukes, Venkat introduce inheritance tax reform legislation for family-owned businesses
Rep. Arvind Venkat
September 10, 2026 | 3:23 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 10 –
This week, state Reps. Brandon Dukes, D-Butler, and Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, introduced legislation that would modernize the family business and family agricultural asset exemption to the state’s inheritance tax.
The legislation (
H.B. 2769
) would reduce the amount of time a family business or family agricultural business must have been in the same family to qualify for an inheritance tax exemption from 7 years to 5 years. The legislation would also increase the maximum amount of assets a qualified family-owned business may have to qualify for an inheritance tax exemption from $5 million to $6.9 million.
Dukes, the prime sponsor of the bill, said that the proposal preserves family businesses while granting much-needed flexibility.
“I know firsthand how much my district relies on the efforts of family-owned establishments, and I want to help them sustain for generations to come,” Dukes said. “That’s why I took on this issue as my first piece of legislation in the House. Every family business has crucial ties to its community, and we need to provide the proper access and resources for these bonds to remain strong.”
Venkat, the co-prime sponsor, echoed that the legislation would fortify the relationship family establishments have with communities in the state.
“Every family business in Pennsylvania has a different story, whether it be a new startup or a staple of the community for generations,” Venkat said. “This legislation will ensure that more family businesses can qualify for inheritance tax exemptions so these establishments can stay where they belong – in our communities and in the family. I look forward to collaborating with Representative Dukes on this legislation that will support the family-owned businesses that keep regions like the North Hills and Cranberry moving.”
An informational hearing of the House Finance Committee on the legislation will take place at a future date
.
For more information on the bill, visit
https://www.palegis.us/legislation/bills/2025/hb2769
.

Legislators pushing for healthcare coverage respond to new PENNIE enrollment numbers
Over 200,000 people disenrolled from health insurance due to federal inaction
Rep. Jen Mazzocco
September 10, 2026 | 9:56 AM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 10 –
Following the release of
new enrollment numbers
under PENNIE, Pennsylvania’s health insurance marketplace, which show significant disenrollments to date in 2026, state Reps. Jen Mazzocco, Arvind Venkat and Steve Samuelson are calling for action on their legislation to increase affordable healthcare coverage in the state.
As of September 2026, 417,000 people are enrolled in PENNIE. In the last nine months, following federal inaction to renew enhanced premium tax credits under the Affordable Care Act, 202,000 people disenrolled. From 2021 to 2025, PENNIE enrollment grew by 150,000, and now net enrollment is down more than 75,000.
The legislators introduced
H.B. 2550
, legislation that would create a state tax credit for small businesses that contribute to their employees’ health coverage. The bill passed the House with
overwhelming bipartisan support
and awaits consideration in the Senate Finance Committee.
“It’s disheartening to see even more Pennsylvanians losing their health insurance,” said
Mazzocco
, prime sponsor of the legislation. “No one in the commonwealth should have to disregard their well-being for financial reasons. I will continue to work alongside my colleagues to make quality affordable healthcare accessible to all and reverse this discouraging enrollment trend.”
Venkat, a board member of PENNIE and the General Assembly’s only elected physician, expressed his concern with these enrollment numbers and urged the Senate to act on H.B. 2550.
“These extremely high disenrollment numbers have one clear cause – the federal government’s inaction to protect the healthcare of Pennsylvanians and Americans,”
Venkat
said. “As an emergency physician, I have seen how access to affordable health insurance can make the difference in whether someone seeks coverage for an illness, which can have life or death ramifications.
“Where federal action is insufficient, it is critical that we act on the state level, which the House has already done. Now, it is the Senate’s turn to support the hundreds of thousands of Pennsylvanians who have lost coverage.”
“It's imperative that our U.S. representatives do their job by reinstating the healthcare credits,” said
Samuelson
, chair of the House Finance Committee. “Meantime, the PA House has responded to offer relief through tax credits to small businesses, and it's now up to our state Senate to do their part and pass the bill to protect Pennsylvanians’ healthcare."

Venkat to introduce legislation to create fairer healthcare contracts
Rep. Arvind Venkat
August 31, 2026 | 9:58 AM
HARRISBURG, Aug. 31 –
In an effort to increase transparency in the healthcare insurance industry, state Rep. Arvind Venkat, the General Assembly’s only elected physician, has announced his
intention to introduce legislation
that will protect healthcare providers from unfair contract changes.
Health insurers and healthcare providers periodically negotiate contracts establishing reimbursement rates, payment methodologies and administrative requirements for covered services. However, many contracts contain unilateral amendment provisions that allow insurers to change these terms during the contract period, often with limited notice to providers.
Venkat’s proposal would prohibit health insurers from unilaterally modifying, amending, or reinterpreting any material condition during the term of a contract with a healthcare provider – ensuring that reimbursements, covered services and payment terms are not changed mid-contract.
“As a physician-legislator who continues to care for patients, I know how critical it is to make sure healthcare is affordable and accessible,” said Venkat, D-Allegheny. “Having our insurers, hospitals and clinicians contracted on an equal basis is crucial in achieving this. This legislation will ensure basic fairness between providers and insurers while protecting healthcare access.”
Venkat is currently circulating the proposal among his colleagues seeking support for the measure and intends to introduce the legislation in the near future.

Venkat secures $100,000 grant for North Boroughs Meals on Wheels
Will support kitchen remodel and equipment upgrades
Rep. Arvind Venkat
August 27, 2026 | 9:44 AM
PITTSBURGH, Aug. 27 –
State Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, announced today that
North Boroughs Meals on Wheels
will be awarded a $100,000 grant to support its operations.
The grant will allow the organization to remodel its kitchen and purchase upgrades for equipment used in the Meals on Wheels program. Funded through a program at the Department of Community and Economic Development, this grant was secured through Venkat’s legislative backing.
“The work that North Boroughs Meals on Wheels does is vital to ensuring that members of our community who need access to nutritious food stay well-fed,” said Venkat. “I am proud to see this funding go to this crucial program that has been supporting communities along the Ohio River for over 30 years.”

PA General Assembly’s only elected physician comments on measles deaths
Deaths mark first in Pennsylvania from the disease in 35 years
Rep. Arvind Venkat
August 25, 2026 | 10:14 AM
HARRISBURG, Aug. 25 –
State Rep. Arvind Venkat, the only elected physician serving in Pennsylvania’s General Assembly, has issued the following statement after two individuals from Lancaster County
died in measles-associated cases
:
“My prayers and deepest condolences are with the families of these two individuals who have died of measles, the first time in Pennsylvania in 35 years,” Venkat said. “Measles is a serious, highly infections and vaccine-preventable illness, and we are facing a worsening outbreak in our Commonwealth.”
Venkat encourages all Pennsylvanians who have not received the measles vaccine to do so, for the safety of themselves and their communities.
“Please speak with your physician and receive the measles vaccine if eligible and have not done so,” Venkat said. “The vaccine is safe and the only effective way to prevent you, your family and your community from suffering from measles.
“Sadly, vaccine policy has become political. Every elected official and those who aspire to lead our communities and Commonwealth should make clear where they stand on immunizations and how to end the growing measles outbreak in Pennsylvania.”
Elected in 2022, Venkat is the first physician to serve in the General Assembly in 60 years. He completed his medical education at Yale University and his emergency medicine residency at the University of Cincinnati/University Hospital. He continues to practice as an emergency physician while serving in elected office.
Along with Reps. Tarik Khan and Bridget Kosierowski, fellow health professional legislators, he is the lead sponsor on
bipartisan legislation
that has passed the state House to protect access to and insurance coverage of vaccines.

Venkat, Grimm Krupa, to introduce legislation to support children of military servicemembers
Will expand tuition assistance for children of those members of the military with extraordinary service records
Rep. Arvind Venkat
August 24, 2026
HARRISBURG, Aug. 24 –
To recognize the extraordinary sacrifices of military servicemembers, state Reps. Arvind Venkat and Charity Grimm Krupa have announced their
intention to introduce bipartisan legislation
that would expand tuition assistance for the children of those members of the military who were certified 100% disabled due to combat, killed-in-action or died as a result of injuries in the line-of-service, awarded the Medal of Honor or Purple Heart, held as a prisoner-of-war, or declared missing-in-action.
Current law, which has not been updated for nearly 40 years, allows the children of veterans with extraordinary service records to receive $500 in tuition assistance for higher education per semester. This new proposal would triple that support to $1,500 per semester and cover gaps in eligibility for federal or state tuition assistance.
“Our military servicemembers and their families have made some of the most difficult sacrifices anyone can,” said Venkat, D-Allegheny. “This legislation will help ease the financial burden on military families and expand access to education while also recognizing the service and sacrifice that protect our freedoms.”
Grimm Krupa has a rich family history of military service. Her father served in the Army, and two of her brothers served in the armed forces -- the Army and the Marine Corps, respectively.
“Freedom has never been free, and the families of our military heroes know that better than most,” said Grimm Krupa, R-Fayette. “When a parent makes the extraordinary sacrifice of serving our nation, that sacrifice is intimately felt by their children as well. I am proud to support this legislation because expanding this educational benefit is a meaningful way to honor that sacrifice and tell these families that Pennsylvania remembers, appreciates and stands with them. We can never fully repay those who have sacrificed to protect our freedom, but we can help give their children the opportunity to build a bright future.”
This legislation, upon introduction, will mark the second bill Venkat has introduced this legislative session to support the education of military families.
Act 32 of 2025
, legislation proposed in collaboration with state Rep. Craig Williams, R-Chester/Delaware, was signed into law by Gov. Josh Shapiro in July of 2025.
Venkat and Grimm Krupa are currently circulating the proposal among their colleagues to seek support for the measure. They intend to introduce the legislation in the near future.

State Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, today announced $2.35 million in grant funding from the

The Pennsylvania House has unanimously passed two bipartisan bills introduced by state Reps. Arvind Venkat and Kristin Marcell that would eliminate administrative burdens to make it easier for physician assistants to receive their licenses.

and
76
would eliminate this redundancy and allow PAs to work under the supervision of either type of doctor, regardless of licensing board.
“As an emergency physician, I have worked hand-in-hand with physician assistants for my entire career. The work they do is absolutely crucial to the delivery of high-quality healthcare,” said Venkat, D-Allegheny. “This legislation will eliminate an unnecessary barrier for PAs to continue doing this lifesaving work. I am thankful to Rep. Marcell for her collaboration on this legislation and to my other colleagues for the overwhelming support for these bills.”
“These bills remove unnecessary red tape and make it easier for physician assistants and physicians to work together in caring for patients," said Marcell, R-Bucks. "I am grateful to Rep. Venkat for his partnership on this effort and pleased to see the House come together in support of a practical change that benefits health care providers, hospitals and the patients they serve."
The two-bill package will now move to the Senate for consideration. During the previous legislative session, both bills received unanimous support both in the House and the relevant Senate committee, but were not considered by the full Senate.

House lawmakers propose bill to protect preventive medical care
Trio of health professional-legislators look to address federal leadership changes
Rep. Arvind Venkat
June 18, 2026 | 1:13 PM
HARRISBURG, June 18 –
As federal officials continue to threaten public health, state Reps. Arvind Venkat, Tarik Khan and Bridget Kosierowski, all healthcare professionals, have
announced their intention to introduce legislation
that would require insurers to continue to cover previously recommended forms of preventive care and allow the Pennsylvania Department of Health to update those recommendations based on the best scientific evidence informed by healthcare professional organizations.
The proposed legislation would require insurers in Pennsylvania to cover all forms of preventive services recommended by the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and the Health Resources and Services Administration as of Jan. 1, 2025. These three agencies have seen significant leadership changes since that time, raising concerns over their independence and scientific credibility.
Under the Affordable Care Act, insurers must cover preventive medical care services recommended by these federal bodies without patient financial responsibility. With the federal changes in these critical entities, Venkat said the validity of their recommendations is very much in question, threatening the insurance coverage of preventive medical care for all Pennsylvanians.
“As a physician-legislator, I have seen how access to evidence-based preventive medical care is under attack,” said Venkat, D-Allegheny. “Due to federal policy and personnel changes, Affordable Care Act-mandated coverage for common screenings and checkups may disappear, harming millions of Pennsylvanians and Americans.
“That is why it’s crucial that we act now to ensure that Pennsylvanians can continue to get the care they need to eliminate their illness in its earliest stages or prevent it in the first place. I am thankful to Reps. Khan and Kosierowski, fellow health professionals, on their partnership on this vital legislation.”
“As a nurse practitioner, I’ve seen firsthand how preventive care saves lives. Early screenings, vaccines and other preventive services help keep people healthy and catch problems before they become more serious,” said Khan, D-Phila. “Since President Trump returned to office, we’ve seen science take a back seat to social media misinformation, conspiracy theories and junk science. That threatens people’s access to lifesaving care and treatment. Our bill protects access to fact-based preventive care so patients can continue getting the screenings, vaccines and treatments they need to stay healthy.”
“As a nurse for 30 years, I repeatedly saw preventive care save lives by catching disease early, and I saw lives lost because patients couldn’t afford screenings or treatment,” said Kosierowski, D-Lackawanna. “I also saw hospitals strained past the breaking point by overwhelming staff workloads and the financial burden of uncompensated care for uninsured patients who had nowhere else to go. This bill will not only protect access to essential, evidence-based preventive care, but it will also help ensure that our healthcare system is not further burdened by growing numbers of uninsured patients.”
In addition to prior recommendations from USPSTF, ACIP and HRSA, the Pennsylvania Department of Health would have the authority to add or remove preventive service requirements based on widely reviewed scientific evidence which would in turn be mandated to be covered by insurers in Pennsylvania without patient financial responsibility.
Common forms of preventive healthcare, which keeps individuals from getting sick and detects conditions in their earliest stages, include vaccinations, cancer screenings and annual checkups, among others.
The legislation comes after the House in October 2025 passed similar legislation introduced by the same group of lawmakers,
H.B. 1828
, to require insurers in Pennsylvania to cover vaccinations recommended by ACIP previously or state health officials and several professional medical societies.
Venkat, Khan and Kosierowski are currently circulating the proposal, seeking the support of their colleagues. The legislation will be introduced shortly.

PA House passes bipartisan bill to protect homeowners
Would require proper disclosures for novel home lending product
Rep. Arvind Venkat
June 2, 2026 | 2:46 PM
HARRISBURG, June 2 –
The Pennsylvania State House has passed bipartisan legislation, 190-11, in favor of regulating shared equity agreements, a novel home lending product, according to the bill’s co-prime sponsors, state Reps.
Arvind Venkat
and
Lindsay Powell
, both D-Allegheny, and
Tim Twardzik
, R-Schuylkill.
Shared Appreciation Agreements are contracts in which a homeowner receives funds in exchange for granting a third party a future interest in the appreciation, equity, or value of their home. The legislation,
H.B. 2120
, would add Shared Equity Agreements to current laws that provide statutory safeguards for other home-secured financial products, such as residential mortgages.
“For most Pennsylvanians, their home is their most valuable asset,”
Venkat
said. “Homeowners may enter into these agreements believing they are making a beneficial decision for their family’s future, but when marketing is unfair or deceptive, they could face significant financial hardship down the road.
“Given the importance of homes and their value to so many Pennsylvanians, we must expeditiously bring shared equity agreements into a regulatory framework similar to that of mortgages so that Pennsylvanians can be assured of transparency and protection against predatory lending practices in these products.”
The legislation would require shared equity agreements to meet disclosure requirements, foreclosure protections, and remedies for violations. Under a shared equity agreement, the more a home appreciates, the more the homeowner must pay to satisfy the contract -- often far exceeding the amount originally received.
“This bill will ensure that homeowners understand the value of their home and how that value will grow over time,” said
Powell
, co-chair of the bipartisan Pennsylvania Housing Caucus. “Intentionally vague language can cost Pennsylvanians a great deal of money in the future just for a short-term gain. We need greater transparency so that our neighbors know what goes into signing onto one of these agreements.”
“As co-chair of the bipartisan Pennsylvania Housing Caucus, I supported this legislation because Pennsylvanians deserve clear, straightforward information when entering complex financial agreements tied to their homes,” said
Twardzik
. “This bill strengthens transparency and establishes important safeguards to protect homeowners while still allowing responsible innovation in the housing finance market.”
The passage of this legislation comes after Point, a company that markets Shared Equity Agreements,
solicited customer feedback
against the legislation with the promise of $50 Amazon gift cards in the lead up to a
House Commerce Committee hearing
on the bill. This came without notice to the committee or any PA House members.
House Bill 2120 will now move to the state Senate for consideration.

Rep. Arvind Venkat
May 20, 2026 | 4:13 PM
HARRISBURG, May 20
– Today, the
PA House Finance Committee
held a public hearing on legislation that would establish a new tax credit for small businesses that contribute to their employees' health insurance premiums.
House Bill 2550
would address affordability and accessibility of healthcare insurance plans for working Pennsylvanians, many of whom lost coverage after enhanced premium tax credits under the Affordable Care Act expired at the end of 2025.
State Rep. Steve Samuleson
, chair of the House Finance Committee and a co-prime sponsor of the bill, said that many small businesses cannot afford to provide group health insurance policies.
“Too many working Pennsylvanians are foregoing health insurance if they can’t access it through their employer,” Samuelson said. “This effort would incentivize small business owners to help their employees by allowing them to claim a tax credit for their contributions. It would keep business moving by keeping employees and their families healthy, reduce leave time due to illness, and give peace of mind to workers with access to quality healthcare.”
Committee member and co-prime sponsor of the bill
Rep. Jen Mazzocco
, D-Allegheny, said that today’s testimony illustrated that small businesses in PA and their employees have a right quality, affordable healthcare.
“With no federal solution in sight, we need to act now at the state level and fill the gaps left by catastrophic ACA cuts,” said Mazzocco. “Our hardworking families shouldn’t have to decide between their health and their wallets, and this bill is a step toward easing that concern.”
Rep. Arvind Venkat
, D-Allegheny, who is a co-prime sponsor of the bill and a practicing emergency physician, testified that action is needed now as the number of uninsured people in PA continues to rise and the specific need with small businesses not offering coverage to their employees.
“With actions at the federal level making it increasingly difficult for Pennsylvania families to afford quality health insurance, we need creative solutions to ensure people are protected,” said Venkat.
“Providing small businesses with a tax credit for contributing to employees’ health insurance premiums would allow business owners to reduce their tax liability and offer the kind of competitive benefits that attract top-notch workers, while at the same time helping more families retain access to critical coverage.”
Alex Halper, senior vice president of government affairs for the Pennsylvania Chamber of Business & Industry, and Dr. David Anderson, assistant professor, Department of Health Services Policy and Management, School of Public Health, University of South Carolina, also testified to how other states are addressing the issue of uninsured workers and how best to ensure health coverage for as many Pennsylvanians as possible while not forgetting the needs of small businesses.
The bill provides that tax credits could be issued only for plans purchased via Pennie, Pennsylvania's health insurance exchange authority. If an employer chooses to participate in the tax credit program, they would be required to make equal contributions to all employees with eligible health insurance costs. This would apply to small businesses with less than 50 employees and would be subject to the personal income tax.
Samuelson said the bill could be scheduled for a committee vote as soon as early June.

Venkat to introduce bill to ensure informed maternal care
Rep. Arvind Venkat
May 11, 2026 | 9:20 AM
HARRISBURG, May 11 –
State Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, today announced his intention to
introduce legislation
that would establish requirements for lay midwives to provide detailed consent forms to patients as they prepare for childbirth.
The legislation would require lay midwives, who do not have to meet training, certification or licensure requirements that licensed Certified Nurse-Midwives and Certified Midwives must meet, to provide informed consent forms to patients that explain the lay midwife’s qualifications and training.
“In the critical time prior to and around giving birth, it is vital that Pennsylvania women have the highest quality of medical care,” said Venkat. “This legislation would ensure that mothers understand the maternal care they are receiving and make the process safer and more transparent to protect both mothers and their babies.”
Consent forms would also require clarification that a lay midwife cannot prescribe medication and that the lay midwife has a written plan to address issues that may occur during labor. The legislation will include an exception for members of religious groups whose practice would be infringed by these requirements.
Venkat is currently circulating the proposal among his colleagues for support. Text of the legislation can be found

State House passes bipartisan legislation to advance geothermal energy development
Rep. Arvind Venkat
May 4, 2026 | 3:49 PM
HARRISBURG, May 4 –
With several states beginning to establish regulations for geothermal energy, Pennsylvania has now joined that group with the state House passing bipartisan legislation to foster the development of this clean base load energy source, announced the bill’s co-prime sponsors, state Reps. Arvind Venkat, Craig Williams and Elizabeth Fiedler.
House Bill 2076
would establish a framework for the development of geothermal energy, which allows for heat deep beneath the Earth's surface to be harnessed for energy from places it previously was not able to be collected. Before recent technological developments, geothermal energy production historically took place near volcanoes and hot springs.
“This legislation will enable us to make bold investments into Pennsylvania’s geothermal resources that we have not been able to use before,”
said Venkat, D-Allegheny
. “We have been a national leader in energy development, and this legislation would enable us to move forward in the world of clean energy production and create jobs, while also reducing energy costs for consumers.”
The framework in this legislation includes several new developments for geothermal energy, including authorizing the state Department of Environmental Protection to regulate geothermal injection wells with a predictable and responsible permitting framework, establish subsurface ownership rights for geothermal resources, and allow for the repurposing of abandoned oil and gas wells for geothermal energy development.
“Pennsylvania faces an electricity crisis as demand rises, and we must focus on increasing generation,”
said Williams, R-Chester/Delaware
. “This legislation creates a path for geothermal energy development by putting existing infrastructure, including legacy oil and gas wells, back into productive use. This bill will strengthen our energy supply and support long-term affordability.”
“As Chair of the House Energy Committee, I am proud to sponsor this bipartisan legislation with Reps. Venkat and Williams that will help move Pennsylvania forward with next generation energy technology,”
said Fiedler, D-Phila.
"Amid our energy crisis and the growing need to meet demand, geothermal energy will diversify Pennsylvania's clean energy portfolio and make us more resilient in years to come."
House Bill 2076 passed 118-83 and now moves to the state Senate for consideration.

Would add second acute care institutional pharmacist and pharmacy technician to the Board of Pharmacy

The Pennsylvania House today unanimously passed bipartisan legislation that would update the membership of the

Venkat on this issue. We remain dedicated to bipartisan collaboration to enhance the well-being of Pennsylvanians.”
House Bill 980 will now move to the state Senate for consideration.

House Energy Committee advances three bills to bring next-generation energy technologies to the Commonwealth
Rep. Arvind Venkat
April 13, 2026 | 4:19 PM
HARRISBURG, April 13
– Today, members of the House Energy Committee voted favorably to report three bills out of committee that would expand energy generation in Pennsylvania and improve grid efficiency.
The bills are:
Geothermal Energy Development, H.B. 2076.
Advanced Transmission Technologies (ATTs), H.B. 2223.
PEDA Modernization, H.B. 2347.
Following a series of public hearings and informational meetings on the Commonwealth’s surging energy needs, state Rep. Elizabeth Fiedler, D-Phila., chair of the House Energy Committee, convened a voting meeting on these key bills.
House Bill 2076, sponsored by Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, and Rep. Craig Williams, R-Chester, earned bipartisan approval with a vote of 15-11. This bill establishes a regulatory framework for geothermal resource production, which could supply millions of homes and businesses with locally sourced, endlessly renewable energy.
Substantial geothermal potential and a robust skilled workforce generate interest in siting projects in the Commonwealth. Pennsylvania currently lacks a regulatory structure for this type of energy production which drives early investment in pilot projects to neighboring states with greater regulatory certainty.
“We all agree that we need more energy production in Pennsylvania,” said Venkat. “Geothermal energy is a new and important way to add clean, base load energy to our grid. Thank you to Chair Fiedler and bipartisan members of the House Energy Committee for approving H.B. 2076, my legislation with Rep. Williams, to provide a framework for developing geothermal energy in our Commonwealth.”
At a public hearing held in March, testifiers noted that H.B. 2076 is critical to maintain the Commonwealth’s competitive edge for public and private investment in geothermal development.
The committee also approved H.B. 2223 and H.B. 2347, both sponsored by Fiedler.
“Pennsylvania is facing a serious energy crisis as rising demand drives up energy costs for the people back home in our districts: working people, seniors, families and small businesses,” Fiedler said. “I’m pleased to see H.B. 2223 and H.B. 2347 advance to the House chamber because these bills are win-win-wins, which would unlock our electric grid’s capacity, build out new, renewable generation resources, and keep costs manageable for everyday people."
House Bill 2223 would enhance the performance of the electric grid by accelerating the adoption of advanced transmission technologies. These software and hardware components on existing grid infrastructure can be completed for a fraction of the cost of building transmission lines, which utility companies would otherwise pass along to their customers.
The bill would ensure that the Commonwealth can accommodate the interconnection of new generation resources needed to reliably meet soaring demand driven by data center development and the electrification of household appliances.
The bill was reported from committee by a vote of 16 -10, earning bipartisan support.
House Bill 2347 would modernize the Pennsylvania Energy Development Authority’s scope and structure to better address PA’s urgent energy development needs. Additionally, the bill changes the authority’s name to the Pennsylvania Energy Financing Authority.
PEDA’s mission is to accelerate the deployment of clean energy and efficiency projects across the Commonwealth. Since PEDA was founded in 1981, the authorizing statute has not been substantially updated. If enacted, H.B. 2347 would expand the types of projects eligible to be financed by PEDA to include new energy generation methods, grid stabilization measures and storage, and grid enhancing technologies.
The measure advanced from committee by a vote of 14-12.
As chair of the House Energy Committee, Fiedler continues to prioritize legislation that attracts innovation and investment in Pennsylvania’s clean energy economy.

Venkat welcomes over $130,000 in new neighborhood assistance funding
Rep. Arvind Venkat
October 19, 2026 | 4:18 PM
PITTSBURGH, Oct. 19 –
State Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, today announced that three projects in the 30th Legislative District will receive funding through the
Neighborhood Assistance Program
, totaling $135,535.
“These funds will support crucial projects in our community that help address housing costs, food insecurity and access to education,” Venkat said. “I am grateful to see these funds come to our community, and I will continue working to ensure that important organizations such as NHCO and Holy Family Institute continue to receive the support they need.”
The projects supported in this funding include:
$81,000
to North Hills Community Outreach to increase emergency assistance to reflect rising housing costs and connect clients to stability and self-sufficiency supports to reduce eviction, homelessness, and repeat financial crises.
NHCO also received
$22,035
to expand access to its three food pantries so clients can visit twice a month as opposed to once a month.
$32,500
to Holy Family Institute for the purchase of a school bus to eliminate transportation barriers and promote access to educational opportunities.
Funding for these projects came through the Neighborhood Assistance Program, a tax-credit program administered by the PA Department of Community and Economic Development that encourages businesses to invest in projects that improve distressed areas.

Ben Avon Heights to receive over $200,000 in grant funding
Will serve for rehabilitation and development of local park
Rep. Arvind Venkat
October 21, 2026 | 3:21 PM
BEN AVON HEIGHTS, Oct. 21 –
Through the
Community Conservation Partnerships Program
, Ben Avon Heights will receive $203,200 in grant funding, announced state Rep. Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, who represents the borough in the state House.
The funding will serve for rehabilitation and development of Ben Avon Heights Park, including construction of pedestrian walkways and a parking area, the installation of play equipment, and landscaping and ADA access improvements on site.
“These improvements will allow our neighbors in Ben Avon Heights to have better opportunities to enjoy nature,” Venkat said. “I look forward to seeing these developments completed, and I will continue to work with my bipartisan colleagues to advocate for state support of our community.”
Venkat worked alongside state Sen. Devlin Robinson, R-Allegheny, to secure this funding.
The grant came through the C2P2 program, which is administered by the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources and serves to build connections between Pennsylvanians and the outdoors by supporting recreational improvements, natural resource conservation, and community revitalization efforts.
